mainTopic: רבי עקיבא laughs while the other חכמים weep: the comfort of seeing a prophecy of destruction come true, which guarantees that the prophecy of redemption will also come true.
overview: The amud opens with the end of the first story. The חכמים hear the noise of Rome and weep, while רבי עקיבא laughs. His reason is a קל וחומר: if God gives so much good to those who go against His will, those who do His will will get far more. Then the גמרא tells a second story. At the ruins of the בית המקדש, the חכמים see a fox come out of the קדש הקדשים and they weep, but רבי עקיבא laughs. He explains with a פסוק in ישעיהו that names אוריה and זכריה together as witnesses. That pairing ties זכריה's prophecy of rebuilding to אוריה's prophecy of destruction. Since the destruction has fully come true, the rebuilding is sure to come true as well. The חכמים answer, 'עקיבא, you have comforted us,' and the הדרן closes the פרק and all of מסכת מכות.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא explains why he laughs at Rome's success
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים finish their complaint that the בית המקדש was burned. רבי עקיבא answers with a קל וחומר: if the wicked get so much, the righteous will get even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...burned by fire, and shall we not weep?!' He said to them: That is exactly why I am laughing. If those who go against His will get all this, those who do His will will surely get much more.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים finish explaining why they are weeping: the בית המקדש lies burned. רבי עקיבא then explains why he is laughing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other חכמים look at Rome's wealth and see only pain. רבי עקיבא draws a קל וחומר from it: God gives this much good to people who do not serve Him, so the reward for those who do His will must be far greater. The very sight that made them cry is his proof of a bright future.

keyTerms.meaning: to those who go against His (God's) will
to those who do His will
how much more so (the wording of a קל וחומר)
laughing

phrases.english: by fire, and shall we not weep?!
phrases.notes: These are the last words of the חכמים's complaint from just before: our בית המקדש is burned by fire.

phrases.english: He said to them: That is why I am laughing.
If for those who go against His will it is like this,

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹשֵׂי רְצוֹנוֹ עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: then for those who do His will, how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first story, which began on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: the wicked prosper this much, so the righteous will prosper even more.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא turns a painful sight into a reason for hope by using a קל וחומר.

steps.title: A fox comes out of the קדש הקדשים
steps.stepSummary: A second story: the חכמים go up to ירושלים, tear their clothes at the sight of the ruins, and see a fox come out of the קדש הקדשים. They weep, and רבי עקיבא laughs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time they were going up to Jerusalem. When they reached Mount Scopus, they tore their clothes. When they reached the Temple Mount, they saw a fox come out of the Holy of Holies. The others began to cry, and רבי עקיבא laughed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about the same חכמים. This step sets the scene for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scene is built to look as hopeless as possible. Even a wild animal walks freely in the holiest place in the world. The story sets up the same contrast as before: they cry and he laughs.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Scopus, the hill from which you first see the site of the בית המקדש
they tore their clothes (a sign of mourning)
the Temple Mount
the Holy of Holies, the innermost room of the בית המקדש
fox

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּב פַּעַם אַחַת הָיוּ עוֹלִין לִירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: Another time, they were going up to Jerusalem.
When they reached Mount Scopus,
they tore their clothes.
When they reached the Temple Mount,
they saw a fox that came out
from the Holy of Holies.
They began to weep,
and Rabbi Akiva was laughing.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב פַּעַם אַחַת הָיוּ עוֹלִין לִירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second story built like the first one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story is set up: a fox in the קדש הקדשים, the חכמים weep, and רבי עקיבא laughs.

steps.title: Why laugh? Why weep?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי עקיבא why he is laughing. He asks them why they are weeping. They explain: a place where even a non-כהן would die for entering now has foxes walking in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Why are you laughing? He said: Why are you crying? They said: This is the place about which it says 'the outsider who comes near shall be put to death,' and now foxes walk in it. Shall we not cry?
steps.whatsHappening: The two sides ask each other why they are reacting this way. The חכמים explain their tears, which sets up רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their pain comes from the contrast. The place was once so holy that a non-כהן entering it deserved death, and now animals walk around in it freely. רבי עקיבא first lets them state their reason so that he can answer it directly.

keyTerms.meaning: an outsider; here, someone who is not a כהן
who comes near shall be put to death
shall we weep

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתָּה מְצַחֵק?
phrases.english: They said to him: Why are you laughing?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתֶּם בּוֹכִים?
phrases.english: He said to them: Why are you weeping?
They said to him: A place about which it is written,
'And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death,'
and now foxes walk in it,
and shall we not weep?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתָּה מְצַחֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the two sides reacted so differently to the scene in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי עקיבא laugh at such a terrible sight?

steps.title: Why are אוריה and זכריה named together?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא quotes a פסוק in ישעיהו that names אוריה and זכריה together as witnesses. He then asks why, since they lived in completely different periods.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: That is why I laugh, because it is written: 'I will take for Myself faithful witnesses, אוריה the כהן and זכריה son of יברכיהו.' What does אוריה have to do with זכריה? אוריה lived in the time of the First Temple, and זכריה in the time of the Second Temple!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא begins his answer by pointing out a puzzle in a פסוק. He is setting up the key idea that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two prophets lived hundreds of years apart, so it is strange for one פסוק to call them witnesses together. This question pushes us to find a deeper link between the two of them.

keyTerms.meaning: faithful, trustworthy witnesses
what does one have to do with the other?
the First Temple
the Second Temple

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: לְכָךְ אֲנִי מְצַחֵק, דִּכְתִיב:
phrases.english: He said to them: That is why I am laughing, as it is written:
'And I will take for Myself faithful witnesses:
Uriah the priest
and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.'

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן אוּרִיָּה אֵצֶל זְכַרְיָה?
phrases.english: Now what does Uriah have to do with Zechariah?
Uriah was in the time of the First Temple,
and Zechariah was in the time of the Second Temple!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן אוּרִיָּה אֵצֶל זְכַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבי עקיבא's answer to the question in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק in ישעיהו 8:2, which lists אוריה and זכריה together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They lived in different eras, so there seems to be no reason to pair them as witnesses.

steps.title: The two prophecies are linked
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers: the פסוק makes זכריה's prophecy depend on אוריה's prophecy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק made זכריה's prophecy depend on אוריה's prophecy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his own question: the two prophets are paired because their prophecies are tied together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two prophets do not share a time period. What they share is a link: one prophecy coming true is a sign that the other will come true too.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק made one thing depend on another
his prophecy

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: תָּלָה הַכָּתוּב נְבוּאָתוֹ שֶׁל זְכַרְיָה
phrases.english: Rather, the verse made the prophecy of Zechariah depend
on the prophecy of Uriah.

steps.terutzResolutionType: A new reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pairing the two prophets seems to have no meaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links זכריה's prophecy to אוריה's prophecy.

steps.title: What each prophet said
steps.stepSummary: אוריה foretold that ציון would be plowed like a field. זכריה foretold that old men and women would once again sit in the streets of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: About אוריה it is written: 'Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field.' About זכריה it is written: 'Old men and old women will once again sit in the streets of Jerusalem.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא quotes the two prophecies he just said are linked: one about destruction and one about rebuilding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אוריה's prophecy describes complete ruin, and that is exactly what the fox shows. זכריה's prophecy describes a peaceful, rebuilt ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: will be plowed like a field
old men and old women
in the streets

phrases.english: About Uriah it is written:
'Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field,'
phrases.notes: מיכה 3:12. The פסוק goes on to say the Temple Mount will become like a forest, which is why a fox there fits it.

phrases.english: About Zechariah it is written:
'Old men and old women will yet sit in the streets of Jerusalem.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two prophecies that step 5 says are linked.

steps.title: The destruction came true, so the rebuilding will too
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that before the destruction fully happened, he worried the rebuilding might not happen. Now that he sees the destruction is complete, he is sure the rebuilding will come.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as אוריה's prophecy had not come true, I was afraid זכריה's prophecy would not come true. Now that אוריה's prophecy has come true, it is certain that זכריה's prophecy will come true.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his full answer to why he laughed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the two prophecies are tied together, the first one coming true guarantees the second. The fox is proof that אוריה's words came true completely. So the sight that made the others cry is, for him, proof that redemption is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: came true; was fulfilled
afraid
it is certain; it is known

steps.whatToRemember: Seeing the prophecy of destruction come true in full is a guarantee that the prophecy of rebuilding will also come true.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not happy about the destruction itself. He is happy because it proves that the promise of rebuilding is sure to come true.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיְּימָה נְבוּאָתוֹ שֶׁל אוּרִיָּה
phrases.english: As long as the prophecy of Uriah had not come true,
I was afraid
that the prophecy of Zechariah would not come true.
Now that the prophecy of Uriah has come true,
it is certain that the prophecy of Zechariah will come true.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיְּימָה נְבוּאָתוֹ שֶׁל אוּרִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the linked prophecies from steps 5 and 6 to answer the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He laughs because the destruction coming true in full proves the rebuilding will come true.

steps.title: Akiva, you have comforted us
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים accept רבי עקיבא's words and say twice that he has comforted them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him, in these words: Akiva, you have comforted us. Akiva, you have comforted us.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the חכמים accepting רבי עקיבא's explanation and being comforted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying it twice shows how deeply they were comforted. Their weeping has turned into hope.

keyTerms.meaning: you have comforted us
with these words

phrases.english: With these words they said to him:
Akiva, you have comforted us; Akiva, you have comforted us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים respond to the answer in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים are comforted: the ruin of the בית המקדש is itself a sign that ירושלים will be rebuilt.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter and finishing the tractate
steps.stepSummary: The traditional הדרן formula closes the פרק אלו הן הלוקין and marks the end of מסכת מכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter "These are the ones who receive lashes," and Tractate מכות is now complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new argument. It is the standard closing line that ends the פרק and announces that all of מסכת מכות is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With הדרן עלך, the learner tells the chapter, 'we will come back to you,' a promise to keep reviewing it. The words וסליקא לה מסכת מכות add that this is the last chapter, so the entire מסכת is now done. The מסכת ends on a hopeful note, right after רבי עקיבא's comfort about the rebuilding of ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the closing formula said when finishing a פרק or מסכת, a commitment to come back and review it
'These are the ones who receive lashes': the name of the third and final פרק of מכות, taken from its opening words
Literally 'it has gone up'. Here it means 'it is finished' or 'it is completed'
The tractate dealing with lashes, עדים זוממין, and the cities of refuge

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת מכות closes with רבי עקיבא's lesson: the destruction of ירושלים has come true, so the promised rebuilding will surely come true too. Then the הדרן seals the מסכת with a promise to return and learn it again.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read הדרן עלך as part of the גמרא's discussion. It is a closing formula that marks the end of the פרק, not a statement by any sage.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "These are the ones who receive lashes"
phrases.notes: That's the name of the third פרק, taken from its first words. We're speaking to the chapter itself.

phrases.english: and Tractate מכות is completed

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ אֵלּוּ הֵן הַלּוֹקִין וּסְלִיקָא לַהּ מַסֶּכֶת מַכּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the חכמים's acceptance of רבי עקיבא's comfort (Step 8) and formally closes the פרק and the מסכת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק אלו הן הלוקין and all of מסכת מכות are complete, with a commitment to return and review them.
